column4: Description
Backend skeleton, data model, authentication, roles, RTL app shell. (PRD 9.1)
Workflow state machine, tool registry, validated outputs, safe failure. Infrastructure for every agent. (PRD 11, 12)
Corpus ingestion, chunking, retrieval, grounded answers with citations, chat UI. (PRD 9.2)
Lawyer-request workflow: intake agent, structured summary, client approval. (PRD 9.3)
Lawyer profiles, deterministic matching, sending requests, accept/decline. (PRD 9.4)
Request inbox, case records, case view, case-context research. (PRD 9.5)
Lawyer-triggered preparation report with provenance and approval. Final system, not January. (PRD 9.6)
Autonomous slot proposal and booking. Secondary priority; must not block January. (PRD 9.7)
Arabic/handwriting OCR experiments, document upload. Supporting/research track. (PRD 9.8)
Threat model, RBAC, tenant isolation, approval gates, audit, prompt-injection defenses and evaluation. Built alongside features. (PRD 10)
Measurable evaluation of retrieval, citations, intake, matching, case prep; lawyer validation; research-contribution decision. (PRD 16)
Integrated vertical slice, demo environment, rehearsal, documentation. (PRD 13, 14, 21)

column3: Set up backend project, CI and core data model
column4:
As a developer, I want a working backend skeleton and core data model, so that all features build on one foundation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repo and CI run automated tests
- Entities exist: users, lawyer profiles, requests, cases, conversations, documents, workflows, audit events
- Seed script creates demo clients and lawyers

column3: Backend repo, env config and CI pipeline
Register and log in as client or lawyer
column4:
As a client or lawyer, I want to register and log in with my role, so that I only see my own workflows.

Acceptance criteria:
- Passwords are hashed
- Tokens/sessions expire
- Role stored and returned at login
- Invalid logins rejected

column3: Register/login endpoints with hashing and token expiry
Review auth: hashing, expiry, brute-force limits

column4:
As a user, I want a consistent Arabic RTL interface, so that every screen feels like one product.

Acceptance criteria:
- RTL layout and shared components
- Navigation differs for client and lawyer roles
- Error and loading states are standardized

column3: RTL layout, theme and shared components

column4:
As the system, I want agent workflows modelled as persisted states, so that approvals and failures are enforced by the backend.

Acceptance criteria:
- States and allowed transitions defined per workflow
- Workflow runs are persisted and resumable
- Invalid transitions are rejected and logged

column3: Define workflow state schema and transitions

column4:
As the system, I want agents to call only registered, permitted tools, so that retrieval never implies write or delete rights.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each tool has a validated input/output schema
- Agents can call only their allowlisted tools
- Denied calls are logged

column3: Tool permission policy (read vs write vs delete)
Enforce permissions in backend with tests
LLM provider abstraction (online or local model)
column4:
As the team, I want models behind one interface, so that the online-vs-local decision does not force a rewrite.

Acceptance criteria:
- Model/provider selected via config
- Feature code does not depend on one vendor
- A local model can be trialled through the same interface

column3: Trial a local model through the interface
Validated structured outputs and safe failure
column4:
As a user, I want the system to ask for clarification or stop safely when AI fails, so that nothing is fabricated.

Acceptance criteria:
- LLM outputs are schema-validated
- Retry then fallback on invalid output
- No missing field is silently invented
- Failures are logged

column3: Choose and ingest the initial Egyptian legal corpus
column4:
As the team, I want a small, verified corpus with metadata, so that retrieval can be built and evaluated.

Acceptance criteria:
- Initial laws chosen with a lawyer's input
- Usage terms of each source recorded
- Ingested with metadata: law, article, source, date

column3: Pick initial laws/sources with a lawyer; record source terms

column4:
As a client, I want my Arabic question to match the right provisions, so that answers are relevant.

Acceptance criteria:
- Chunks follow article/provision boundaries
- Normalization covers alef/ya/ta marbuta variants, diacritics, tatweel
- Unit tests exist

column3: Compare two chunking strategies on a small question set
Retrieval service returning passages with source metadata
column4:
As a developer, I want one retrieval API, so that chat, intake and lawyer research share it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Takes query and filters, returns top-k passages with law/article/source
- Latency logged

column3: Legal chat UI with citations and source panel
column4:
As a client, I want to see exactly which law supports each answer, so that I can trust and verify it.

Acceptance criteria:
- RTL chat interface
- Citation opens passage with law, article and text
- Disclaimer always visible
- Loading and error states

column3: Citation chips and source passage panel

column4:
As a client, I want answers backed by retrieved sources, so that I am not given invented law.

Acceptance criteria:
- Substantive claims link to passages or are marked unsupported
- Disclaimer included in every answer

column3: State 'cannot answer reliably' when sources are insufficient
column4:
As a client, I want to be told when the system lacks sources, so that I am not misled.

Acceptance criteria:
- Low retrieval confidence triggers a clear refusal
- Tested on out-of-corpus questions
- No fabricated citations

As the team, I want to test reranking, so that we add it only if metrics show it helps.

Acceptance criteria:
- Hit@5 compared with and without reranking
- Decision recorded

column3: Compare against baseline and record decision
Client starts a lawyer request from the chat
column4:
As a client, I want to request a lawyer after getting an answer, so that my problem moves to a professional.

Acceptance criteria:
- 'Request a Lawyer' starts the intake workflow
- Chat context carries over
- Workflow state is INTAKE

column3: Request a Lawyer entry point in the client UI
Define intake workflow states with P1
Intake agent: classify niche and collect case facts
column4:
As a client, I want the agent to ask for what a lawyer needs, so that I describe my case completely.

Acceptance criteria:
- Niche chosen from a controlled list
- Collects facts, dates, parties, urgency and budget
- Asks follow-up questions when something is missing
- Unknown information is stored as 'not provided'

column3: Controlled niche list agreed with a lawyer

column4:
As a client, I want intake to end when it is complete or I have nothing to add, so that I am not stuck in a loop.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ends when required fields are complete or the client says so
- Max-turn fallback exists

column3: Generate and validate structured case summary
column4:
As a lawyer, I want a structured summary that matches what the client said, so that I can trust it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Summary generated only from the conversation
- Validator checks each fact against the conversation
- Mismatches flagged, unknowns stay 'not provided'

column3: Intake test set of 15 sample conversations
Client reviews, edits and approves the summary
column4:
As a client, I want to control what is sent to a lawyer, so that I decide what I share.

Acceptance criteria:
- Client can edit the summary
- Approval is an explicit backend state
- Nothing reaches a lawyer before approval
- Approval is logged

column3: Send approved request to a lawyer
column4:
As a client, I want to send my approved summary to a lawyer, so that I can get help.

Acceptance criteria:
- January version: client picks a lawyer from a simple seeded list
- Request carries the approved summary
- Status becomes SENT

column3: Lawyer accepts or declines; client sees status
column4:
As a lawyer, I want to accept or decline, and the client to be told, so that requests are handled quickly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Accept and decline transitions work
- Client sees current status
- Both actions are logged

column3: Lawyer profile: niches, budget range, availability
column4:
As a lawyer, I want to define my niches and fees, so that I receive suitable requests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Lawyer can create and edit a profile
- Niches come from the controlled list

As a client, I want suitable lawyers listed with clear reasons, so that I can choose with confidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Filters by niche and budget; availability optional
- Explanations use only profile data
- No paid placement
- Unit tests for rules

column3: Reuse approved summary after decline or expiry
column4:
As a client, I want to resend my approved summary to another lawyer, so that I do not repeat intake.

Acceptance criteria:
- Declined/expired requests can be resent
- Previous approval is kept

As a lawyer, I want an inbox of structured requests, so that I can decide quickly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Shows approved structured summary
- Filter by status
- Only my requests are visible

column3: Inbox list and request detail screens

column4:
As a lawyer, I want an accepted request to become a case, so that work has a home.

Acceptance criteria:
- Acceptance creates a case from the approved summary
- Conversation is linked
- Audit event written

column3: Basic case page: facts and summary
Full case workspace: timeline, conversations, documents, saved research
column4:
As a lawyer, I want all case material in one place, so that I can prepare efficiently.

Acceptance criteria:
- Timeline and linked conversations shown
- Saved research listed
- Documents tab shown where supported

column3: Source-backed legal research using case context
column4:
As a lawyer, I want research that uses my case facts, so that I find relevant provisions and rulings.

Acceptance criteria:
- Retrieves provisions and similar rulings
- Every result shows its source
- Needs case-law data (confirmed available)

As a lawyer, I want to save useful research, so that it stays with the case.

Acceptance criteria:
- Save and remove research items
- Only the case's lawyer can access them

As a lawyer, I want to start preparation myself, so that no AI work happens without my command.

Acceptance criteria:
- Only the case's lawyer can start it
- Agent reads authorized case data only

column3: Verify the agent reads only authorized data; test

column4:
As a lawyer, I want the agent to find issues and relevant law, so that I save research time.

Acceptance criteria:
- Issues extracted from case facts
- Provisions and similar rulings retrieved per issue

column3: Provision and ruling retrieval per issue

column4:
As a lawyer, I want a report with sources, so that I can verify every legal claim.

Acceptance criteria:
- Sections: issues, provisions, precedents, arguments, weak points, missing information
- Each legal claim has source provenance

column3: Lawyer edits and approves report as case artifact
column4:
As a lawyer, I want AI output to stay a proposal until I approve it, so that I keep control.

Acceptance criteria:
- Lawyer can edit
- Explicit approval creates the artifact
- Versions and approval are logged

column3: Lawyer availability and client preferred times
column4:
As a lawyer or client, I want to state when I am available, so that meetings can be planned.

Acceptance criteria:
- Lawyer availability stored
- Client preferred times captured

As a client, I want to receive available slots after a lawyer accepts and pick one, so that booking is effortless.

Acceptance criteria:
- Triggered on acceptance, no lawyer approval step (decided)
- Mutual slots computed and sent to client
- No double booking under concurrent requests
- Cancellation restarts the same flow
- Booking and cancellation logged

column3: Restrict scheduling agent to calendar tools only

column4:
As the team, I want measured OCR quality, so that we decide whether OCR becomes a research contribution.

Acceptance criteria:
- Evaluation set with ground truth (non-sensitive, synthetic or consented)
- At least two approaches compared
- CER/WER reported
- Recommendation written

column3: Build evaluation set and ground truth
Run OCR candidates and record CER/WER
Preprocessing pipeline for scans and handwriting
column4:
As the team, I want preprocessing, so that OCR accuracy improves.

Acceptance criteria:
- Deskew, denoise, binarize options tested
- Effect on CER/WER measured

As a client, I want to upload a document, so that I can attach it to my request.

Acceptance criteria:
- Upload and preview work
- Files are ownership-protected
- Unsafe file types rejected

column3: Secure file storage with ownership checks
Show OCR confidence to the user
column4:
As a lawyer, I want to see OCR uncertainty, so that I know what to double-check.

Acceptance criteria:
- Low-confidence regions highlighted

As the team, I want a threat model early, so that security shapes the design instead of being added later.

Acceptance criteria:
- Assets, actors and trust boundaries documented
- Abuse cases for chat, intake, requests, case prep and scheduling
- Each abuse case maps to a control
- Reviewed with the team before Sprint 3

As a user, I want to access only what I am authorized for, so that private data stays private.

Acceptance criteria:
- Client and lawyer routes separated
- Ownership verified on protected resources
- Unauthorized access returns 403 and is tested

column3: Ownership checks on requests, cases, conversations
Approval gates as backend workflow states
column4:
As a lawyer or client, I want sensitive actions blocked until I approve, so that AI never acts silently.

Acceptance criteria:
- List of approval-required actions exists
- Direct calls without approval are rejected
- Approval records user and time

column3: Approval transitions in the state machine

column4:
As a user, I want retrieval to respect data boundaries, so that nobody sees another user's material.

Acceptance criteria:
- Retrieval filters applied at query time
- Cross-user retrieval attempt returns nothing
- Tested

column3: Audit trail of AI and human actions
column4:
As a lawyer, I want important actions recorded, so that I can trace what happened.

Acceptance criteria:
- Events: AI proposals, tool calls, approvals, request transitions, case edits
- Append-only
- Includes actor, time, workflow id

As the system, I want client text, documents and retrieved text treated as data, so that injected instructions do not control agents.

Acceptance criteria:
- Untrusted text passed in delimited data sections
- No tool runs on instructions found in untrusted text
- Pattern documented

column3: Apply to chat, intake and RAG chains
Security evaluation dataset and baseline attack success rate
column4:
As the team, I want a repeatable attack set, so that we can measure defenses before and after.

Acceptance criteria:
- Covers prompt injection, malicious documents and authorization bypass
- At least 50 cases
- Baseline attack success rate recorded before defenses

As the team, I want defenses compared with the baseline, so that we can show measured improvement.

Acceptance criteria:
- Defenses implemented
- Before/after attack success rate compared
- Findings written up

As a lawyer, I want to see the audit timeline for a request or case, so that actions are visible.

Acceptance criteria:
- Timeline shows actor, action, time
- Only authorized users can view

column3: Audit query API with ownership checks
Lawyer interviews: intake fields, niches and corpus
column4:
As the team, I want lawyers to check our assumptions, so that we build the right thing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake required fields confirmed
- Niche list confirmed
- Initial corpus reviewed

column3: Interview on intake fields and niches
Review corpus and sample Q&A with a lawyer
Retrieval evaluation set and Hit@5 baseline
column4:
As the team, I want measured retrieval quality, so that improvements are evidence-based.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least 30 Arabic questions with lawyer-checked relevant articles
- Hit@5 reported

As the team, I want to know if cited passages support the claims, so that grounding is proven.

Acceptance criteria:
- Manual rubric defined
- Sample of answers reviewed
- Supported vs unsupported claim rate reported

As the team, I want intake quality measured, so that we know the agent preserves facts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Required-field completeness measured
- Factual preservation measured
- Unsupported-information rate measured

As the team, we need to commit to our research contribution(s), so that effort concentrates on them.

Acceptance criteria:
- Options reviewed: secure agents, RAG/citations, agent evaluation, OCR
- OCR decision made using the benchmark result
- Decision written down and agreed with the supervisor

column3: Prepare options with evidence so far

column4:
As the team, we want lawyers to assess case-prep output, so that usefulness is measured.

Acceptance criteria:
- Lawyer rates usefulness, source correctness, issue identification, missing information

As the team, I want a simple screen for running and reviewing evaluations, so that results are easy to inspect.

Acceptance criteria:
- Shows evaluation runs and metrics

column3: Integrate the end-to-end January vertical slice
column4:
As the team, I want the whole flow working together, so that the January demo is a real slice, not separate screens.

Acceptance criteria:
- Login, question, cited answer, request a lawyer, intake, summary, approval, lawyer inbox, accept, case, audit trail all run on the deployed environment
- No manual database edits needed

column3: Integration plan and contract tests between modules
Demo scenario, seeded data and rehearsal
column4:
As the team, I want a rehearsed demo, so that January goes smoothly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Scripted scenario
- Seeded demo users and lawyers
- Fallback plan if a service fails
- Full dry run

As the team, I want a lawyer to review the demo, so that we get feedback before presenting.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least one lawyer sees the demo
- Feedback recorded as backlog items

As the team, we need each core AI feature documented with its limits, so that Definition of Done is met.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each core AI feature has a short doc: what it does, how it is tested, known limits
